desc: a sunday service for seekers of the sacred across every path.
The Hearth is the simplest sacred technology: a living center we tend to together. It belongs to no one, yet it warms everyone.

sharing aloud the passages or poems that moved us in our reading

projects.name: a container to share opinions that will get you cancelled
desc: The purpose of the workshop was to create a field where people could share charged truths and stay in embodied presence with difference. The invitation was not to convince or negate others, but to share the life experiences, ancestral threads, and cultural conditioning that gave rise to each person's view.

video.title: a container for hot takes @ harvard

steps.title: Musical intro 🎵🎻
steps.text: Gather in circle for a cello performance

steps.title: Introduction
items: Why we’re here: to be seen, and share without judgement
Talk less about your opinion, but the specific life experiences you had that led to that opinion

steps.title: Participatory co-creation of controversial themes we’d want to discuss
steps.text: “What’s an issue you sometimes struggle to share in public or what’s one of your most controversial takes that would be unpopular?” i.e. I have certain anti-capitalist views like limits on wealth,
items: Everybody writes down their opinion and puts it in a hat
Hat gets handed around and each person reads themes out loud
Theme gets put into WhatsApp for crowd voting
Top 2 voted on topics are subsequent discussion topics

steps.title: Round #1: Forming Triads
steps.text: Randomly assign people into groups of three.

steps.title: Full-Group Reflections
items: What surprised you? What did you enjoy? What was challenging

projects.name: council of the cosmos
projects.tagline: re-enchanting the pursuit of multiple truths
desc: Council of the Cosmos is a structured role-play workshop designed to help participants explore multiple, often conflicting, ways of knowing through embodied perspective-taking.
images: the archetype cards (the politician, the elder, the priestess, the philosopher, the scientist, the mystic, the artist, the farmer, the revolutionary) beside a phenomenon card and a candle
Council of the Cosmos booklets fanned out beside a candle and incense
a participant writing in her council booklet

images.alt: a short clip moving over the archetype cards, candle and incense

slides.title: the slides that guided the council
images: Council of the Cosmos Re-enchanting the Pursuit of Multiple Truths
In the near future... In times of need, a council is called to discussed earthly and cosmological matters
Representatives from all walks of life are invited to share their perspectives and discuss ways to move forward

As a member of the council, you represent an archetype, a particular way of knowing and living To find your archetype, draw three cards and select one to represent throughout this workshopand meditate if you wish Setting the stage

A moment to step into your archetype’s shoes • Scan the QR code on your chosen card to listen to stories about your archetype • Take a moment to close your and meditate if you wish Getting into character (7 min)

Based on the stories, the information on the card, and your extrapolations think of where this archetype might inhabit, what they might be called • Draw or write a description of where your archetype might inhabit • What meaning do the tools on your card reveal to you? Share out (10 min)
• Share one thing you have discovered about your character with the group Share out (10 min)
The oldest participant of the council draws a card from the Phenomenon card deck and reads it out loud to the group A strange phenomenon occurs
From your archetype’s perspective, elaborate a possible explanation for this phenomenon • What might have caused it? • Does it pose a risk? • Should anything be done about it? Explanation (5 min)
The Council convenes... • Share your explanation with the group and how you came to it • Engage with other participants to understand their perspectives Discussion (10 min)

Having listened to the different perspectives on the phenomenon at hand, Council members determine whether any interference is necessary • Did the discusison shift your perspective or has it reinforced your original point of view? • Are there value systems of others that are particularly complementary or averse to the ones you hold? Next Steps (10 min)
The youngest member of the council reads the backside of the phenomenon card in play to the group The strange phenomenon intensifies...

Response (10min) Using the unique mediums at the disposal of each archetype, council members asses how to move forward given the recent aggravation • How do you move forward from here now that it’s a crisis from your point of view? (use your objects) • Write the explanation out in your book
Discussion (10min) The Council convenes again... • Share your explanation with the group and how you came to it • Engage with other participants to understand their perspectives

Conclusion (10min) As you let go of your archetype, reflect on and share what you might have learned through this experience “What treasure from your archetype other archetypes do you want to keep alive in your own life?”

press.title: a salon for ‘nones’
press.desc: Maggie Phillips profiles The Commons as a “fourth place” for the religion-curious: atheists, agnostics, and the spiritual but not religious who gather in Hayes Valley for salons, meditation, potlucks, and concerts. The piece follows how it grew from a 2022 GoFundMe into a campus of courses, guilds, and practicums.

press.title: words that matter, issue 16
press.desc: I was the guest curator for this issue of Matter’s newsletter, sharing the words that have mattered most to me, from Joan Didion’s “On Self-Respect” and Annie Dillard’s “Living Like Weasels” to Tanizaki’s “In Praise of Shadows” and Christopher Alexander. It also spotlights The Commons and Rabbit Holes.

press.title: my desk setup and home workspace
press.desc: A peek at my desk and the rhythm of a day: coffee and a 30-minute sit at 6am, a morning on whatever feels most alive, afternoons at The Commons, and evenings at a salon, circle, or workshop. My one rabbit hole recommendation: your own answer to “Who am I?”
